items.title: Joint smoothness of the spherical-mean family of a smooth spacetime function
items.reference: completed-expansion-arguments.md#W1-W3 (scaffolder-added prerequisite for the source term of thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff)
items.design_state: complete-local-branch-argument; added by this scaffolder as a necessary prerequisite, recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), declared by the surface-integral and parameter-integral conventions below. Let $t_0<T$ and let $h\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T])$ in the extension sense: $h$ is the restriction of a $C^\infty$ function on $\mathbb R^3\times J$ for some open interval $J\supset[t_0,T]$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Let $d\Omega$ be the surface measure on the unit sphere $S^2\subset\mathbb R^3$ of total mass $\int_{S^2}d\Omega=4\pi$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), and define the spherical-mean family $$M(x,s,v):=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{S^2}h(x+sn,v)\,d\Omega(n),\qquad (x,s,v)\in\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\times[t_0,T].$$ Then $M$ is of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\times[t_0,T]$ in the same extension sense, and for every multi-index $\alpha$ in $x$ and all integers $m,l\ge0$ $$D_x^\alpha\partial_s^m\partial_v^lM(x,s,v)=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{S^2}D_x^\alpha\partial_s^m\partial_v^l\bigl[h(x+sn,v)\bigr]\,d\Omega(n),$$ where the right-hand integrand is the corresponding iterated partial derivative of the composed map $(x,s,v)\mapsto h(x+sn,v)$; in particular $\partial_s[h(x+sn,v)]=\nabla_x h(x+sn,v)\cdot n$, where $\nabla_xh(y,v):=(\partial_{y_0}h(y,v),\partial_{y_1}h(y,v),\partial_{y_2}h(y,v))\in\mathbb R^3$ is the spatial gradient at fixed $v$, so the $s$-derivatives are directional derivatives along $n$. Consequently, for every $c>0$ the map $\tilde H(x,t,v):=(t-v)\,M(x,c(t-v),v)$ is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]\times[t_0,T]$ in the extension sense, and for every fixed $x\in\mathbb R^3$ the map $(t,v)\mapsto\tilde H(x,t,v)$ is $C^\infty$ on an open neighbourhood of the closed triangle $\{(t,v):t_0\le v\le t\le T\}$. Nothing here assumes decay, compact support or boundedness of $h$; the statement is local in $(x,s,v)$ and uses uniform bounds only on compact parameter sets.
items.strategy: Fix a point $(x_0,s_0,v_0)$ and a compact parameter box $K_x\times S\times V$ around it. The composed integrand $(x,s,v,n)\mapsto h(x+sn,v)$ is $C^\infty$ jointly on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\times[t_0,T]\times S^2$ by the chain rule applied to the affine map $(x,s,v,n)\mapsto x+sn$ and the projection $(x,v)\mapsto(x,v)$, its partial derivatives being the corresponding iterated partial derivatives of $h$ evaluated at $(x+sn,v)$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Prove by induction on the total order $N=|\alpha|+m+l$ that all partial derivatives of $M$ through order $N$ exist and are continuous on $K_x\times S\times V$ and that the displayed differentiated-integral formula holds at that order: the surface clause of the parameter-integral lemma ([[lem-em-parameter-integrals]], used with the fixed compact $C^1$ hypersurface $S^2$ and with each of the parameter directions $x_j$, $s$, $v$ in turn) states that the sphere integral is continuously differentiable in the chosen parameter with derivative equal to the sphere integral of the corresponding partial derivative of the composed integrand, because $h$ and all of its partial derivatives are continuous on the compact set $S^2\times K_x\times S\times V$; since the differentiated integrand is again $C^\infty$ jointly, the procedure can be iterated through all parameter directions in any order, which gives existence and continuity of every partial derivative through order $N$, together with the displayed formula at that order (the $s$-derivatives of $h(x+sn,v)$ are the corresponding directional derivatives along $n$, by the chain rule). As $N$ is arbitrary, $M$ is $C^\infty$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]); the dependence on the parameters is local, so no decay or support condition on $h$ is used. The final claims follow by composing with the smooth affine map $(t,v)\mapsto(t-v,c(t-v),v)$ and multiplying by the smooth factor $t-v$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]); the Axiom of Countable Choice is carried from the sphere-integral convention under which the integrals are read ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[def-countable-choice]]).

items.title: The three-dimensional wave Cauchy problem: Kirchhoff representation, uniqueness, domain of dependence and compact support
items.design_state: complete-exact-declared-branch-conditional-research-argument; published imported wave suppliers routed in place of the design's older distributional edge
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), used through the cited published suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $c>0$, $t_0\in\mathbb R$, $T>t_0$, let $a,b\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ and let $h\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T])$ in the extension sense that $h$ is the restriction of a $C^\infty$ function on $\mathbb R^3\times J$ for some open interval $J\supset[t_0,T]$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Write $W:=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$, so that $c^2W=\Box_c$ is the wave operator of speed $c$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[def-wave-equation-cauchy-data-and-wave-speed]]). For $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ and $s\ge0$ let $H_\varphi(x,s):=s\,M_{cs}\varphi(x)$, where $M_r\varphi(x)=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{S^2}\varphi(x+rn)\,d\Omega(n)$ is the spherical mean of [[lem-em-spherical-mean-wave-identity]]. Define, with $s=t-t_0$, $$u(x,t):=\partial_sH_a(x,s)+H_b(x,s)+c^2\int_{t_0}^{t}H_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv,\qquad (x,t)\in\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T],$$ where $h(\cdot,v)$ denotes the map $x\mapsto h(x,v)$ and $\partial_sH_a$ is the partial derivative of $H_a$ in its second argument, evaluated at $s=t-t_0$. Then:

(a) $u$ is of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ in the extension sense, $Wu=h$ on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$ (indeed on the open neighbourhood of the closed time interval on which the extension of $h$ is defined), $u(\cdot,t_0)=a$ and $\partial_tu(\cdot,t_0)=b$.

(b) Uniqueness: every $v\in C^2(\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T])$ in the extension sense with $Wv=h$ on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$, $v(\cdot,t_0)=a$ and $\partial_tv(\cdot,t_0)=b$ equals $u$.

(c) Domain of dependence: let $\tilde a,\tilde b\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$, $\tilde h\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T])$ and let $\tilde u$ be the corresponding solution. If $\tilde a=a$ and $\tilde b=b$ on the closed ball $\overline B_{c(t_*-t_0)}(x_*)$ and $\tilde h=h$ on the closed backward cone $K(x_*,t_*):=\{(y,v)\in\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,t_*]:|y-x_*|\le c(t_*-v)\}$ ([[def-forward-and-backward-wave-cones-domain-of-dependence-and-influence]]), then $\tilde u(x_*,t_*)=u(x_*,t_*)$ for every $x_*\in\mathbb R^3$ and $t_*\in[t_0,T]$.

(d) Compact support: if $a$ vanishes off a compact $K_a\subset\mathbb R^3$, $b$ vanishes off a compact $K_b$, and $h(\cdot,v)$ vanishes off a fixed compact $K_h$ for every $v\in[t_0,T]$, then for every $t\in[t_0,T]$ the function $u(\cdot,t)$ has compact spatial support: if $K_a\cup K_b\cup K_h\subseteq\overline B_\rho(0)$ for some $\rho>0$ (which exists, [[thm-heine-borel-rn]]), then $u(x,t)=0$ whenever $|x|>\rho+c(t-t_0)$.

No boundary condition on a finite spatial domain, no finite-total-energy hypothesis, and no decay of $a,b,h$ at infinity is assumed or asserted.
items.strategy:
Time translation $t\mapsto t-t_0$ (chain rule) reduces the proof to $t_0=0$; the operator and the formula are invariant under it. Decompose $u=u_h+u_s$ with $u_h:=\partial_sH_a(x,s)+H_b(x,s)$ and $u_s:=c^2\int_{t_0}^{t}H_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv$, $s=t-t_0$.

(1) Smoothness. By [[lem-em-spherical-mean-family-smoothness]] the map $(x,s,v)\mapsto M(x,s,v)=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{S^2}h(x+sn,v)\,d\Omega(n)$ is $C^\infty$ jointly, hence so is $(x,t,v)\mapsto H_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)=(t-v)M(x,c(t-v),v)$ on the region $t_0\le v\le t\le T$, and for fixed $x$ it is $C^\infty$ near the closed triangle $t_0\le v\le t\le T$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). For the same reason $u_h\in C^\infty$, and for fixed $x$ the integrand $v\mapsto H_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)$ is $C^\infty$ on $[t_0,t]$; the fixed-interval clause of [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] differentiates $u_s$ in $x$ under the integral sign, and [[lem-derivative-of-an-integral-with-moving-endpoints]] differentiates it in $t$ with the endpoint terms. Iterating these two steps (each differentiated integrand is again $C^\infty$ jointly) gives $u_s\in C^\infty$ and $u\in C^\infty$ in the extension sense.

(2) Equation and initial data. [[lem-em-spherical-mean-wave-identity]] gives, for every $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$, $\partial_t^2H_\varphi=c^2\Delta H_\varphi$ for $t\ge0$, $H_\varphi(\cdot,0)=0$ and $\partial_tH_\varphi(\cdot,0)=\varphi$. Hence $\partial_t^2(\partial_sH_a)=\partial_s(\partial_t^2H_a)=c^2\Delta\partial_sH_a$ and $\partial_t^2H_b=c^2\Delta H_b$, so $\partial_t^2u_h=c^2\Delta u_h$; here $\partial_s$ commutes with $\Delta$ on $C^\infty$ functions ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]) and $\Delta$ is linear ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]). Also $u_h(\cdot,t_0)=a$, $\partial_tu_h(\cdot,t_0)=b$ because $\partial_s^2H_a(\cdot,0)=c^2\Delta H_a(\cdot,0)=0$. For $u_s$, two applications of [[lem-derivative-of-an-integral-with-moving-endpoints]] at fixed $x$ give $\partial_tu_s=c^2\int_{t_0}^t\partial_tH_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv$ (the endpoint term $H_{h(\cdot,t)}(x,0)$ vanishes) and $\partial_t^2u_s=c^2\bigl[\partial_tH_{h(\cdot,t)}(x,0)+\int_{t_0}^t\partial_t^2H_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv\bigr]=c^2h(x,t)+c^2\int_{t_0}^tc^2\Delta_xH_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv$; differentiating in $x$ under the integral sign with [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] gives $\Delta u_s=c^2\int_{t_0}^t\Delta_xH_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv$, so $\partial_t^2u_s=c^2h+c^2\Delta u_s$, i.e. $Wu_s=h$. Finally $u_s(\cdot,t_0)=0$ and $\partial_tu_s(\cdot,t_0)=0$ because $H_\varphi(\cdot,0)=0$. Adding the two parts gives (a); note the normalisation $c^2W=\Box_c$ is what places the factor $c^2$ on the source integral.

(3) Uniqueness and domain of dependence. If $v$ is a second $C^2$ solution with the same data, then $w:=u-v$ solves $\Box_cw=0$ on a neighbourhood of $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ and has $w(\cdot,t_0)=\partial_tw(\cdot,t_0)=0$. Fix $(x_*,t_*)$ with $t_*>t_0$ and shift time; on the closed backward cone of [[def-forward-and-backward-wave-cones-domain-of-dependence-and-influence]] the functions $w$ and the zero solution satisfy the hypotheses of [[thm-domain-of-dependence-and-local-uniqueness]] (zeros agree, and the sources $0$ agree), so $w\equiv0$ on that cone and in particular $w(x_*,t_*)=0$; as $(x_*,t_*)$ is arbitrary, $w=0$. Claim (c) is the same argument applied to $u-\tilde u$, whose data agree on the base ball $\overline B_{c(t_*-t_0)}(x_*)$ and whose source vanishes on the cone.

(4) Compact support. In the displayed formula for $u(x,t)$ each term integrates over spheres of radius $cs$ or $c(t-v)$, $0\le t-v\le t-t_0$, centred at $x$, the integrands being $a,\nabla a,b$ or $h(\cdot,v)$; if $\overline B_{c(t-t_0)}(x)$ does not meet $K:=K_a\cup K_b\cup K_h$, all these integrals vanish and $u(x,t)=0$. If $K\subseteq\overline B_\rho(0)$ and $|x|>\rho+c(t-t_0)$, then every $y\in\overline B_{c(t-t_0)}(x)$ has $|y|\ge|x|-c(t-t_0)>\rho$, so $\overline B_{c(t-t_0)}(x)\cap K=\emptyset$ and $u(x,t)=0$; the existence of $\rho$ is the boundedness of the compact set $K$ ([[thm-heine-borel-rn]]), which also gives that $\overline B_{\rho+c(t-t_0)}(0)$ is compact. This proves (d) and completes the proof.

items.title: Worked checks of the wave Cauchy formula: source non-compactness, support propagation and linear growth
items.reference: batch-17-local-construction (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-17.notes.md); the design reserves no example for this B page, and this example checks clauses (a), (b) and (d) of thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]] and its suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]]). All three computations use the notation of that theorem: $c>0$, $H_\varphi(x,s)=s\,M_{cs}\varphi(x)$ with the spherical mean $M$ of [[lem-em-spherical-mean-wave-identity]], $W=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$ and $u$ the solution displayed there.

(i) (The compact-support clause needs its hypothesis.) Take $t_0=0$, $a=b=0$ and the spatially constant source $h(x,t)=1$ on $\mathbb R^3\times[0,T]$. Then the theorem's solution is $u(x,t)=c^2t^2/2$, which is independent of $x$; it satisfies $\partial_t^2u=c^2=c^2h$ and $\Delta u=0$, hence $Wu=h$, with $u(\cdot,0)=\partial_tu(\cdot,0)=0$. For every $t>0$ the function $u(\cdot,t)=c^2t^2/2$ is a nonzero constant on $\mathbb R^3$, so it is not compactly supported: the hypothesis in clause (d) that $h(\cdot,v)$ vanish off one fixed compact set cannot be dropped, and the corresponding hypothesis of [[thm-wave-duhamel-principle]] (source compactly supported in $x$ for each fixed $s$) is genuinely used by that item.

(ii) (Support propagation made explicit.) Take $a=b=0$, $t_0=0$ and $h(x,t)=h_0(x)$ with $h_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ vanishing off $\overline B_1(0)$. Then $u(x,t)=c^2\int_0^t(t-v)M_{c(t-v)}h_0(x)\,dv$, and $M_rh_0(x)=0$ for every $r>0$ with $S_r(x)\cap\overline B_1(0)=\emptyset$; hence $u(x,t)=0$ whenever $|x|>1+ct$. This is clause (d) with $K_h=\overline B_1(0)$ and $\rho=1$, exhibited from the explicit formula.

(iii) (The class contains non-decaying data with divergent total energy.) Take $a=0$, $b(x)=x_1$ and $h=0$. Since the first moment of the unit-sphere measure vanishes, $M_{cs}b(x)=x_1$ ([[lem-first-moment-of-the-unit-sphere-vanishes]], with the surface measure identified with the polar measure of [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]), so the theorem's solution is $u(x,t)=(t-t_0)x_1$: it satisfies $\partial_t^2u=0=\Delta u$, hence $Wu=0$, with $u(\cdot,t_0)=0$ and $\partial_tu(\cdot,t_0)=x_1$. The solution is unbounded on every time slice $t>t_0$. Moreover its total energy at time $t$ in the sense of [[def-wave-energy-and-energy-flux]] is $+\infty$ whenever $t\ne t_0$: the energy density is $\tfrac12(x_1^2+c^2(t-t_0)^2)$, and for every $R>0$ the box $[-R,R]^3$ gives $$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\tfrac12\bigl(x_1^2+c^2(t-t_0)^2\bigr)\,d\lambda\;\ge\;\frac12\int_{[-R,R]^3}x_1^2\,d\lambda\;=\;\frac12\Bigl(\frac{2R^3}{3}\Bigr)(4R^2)\;=\;\frac{4}{3}R^5\longrightarrow+\infty$$ ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]], [[thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). Hence the finite-initial-energy hypothesis of [[cor-energy-uniqueness-for-the-wave-cauchy-problem]] fails for this smooth datum while the theorem's local uniqueness (b) still applies; the theorem asserts no decay at spatial infinity and no finite-energy property, and needs none.
items.strategy:
All three clauses are direct substitutions into the displayed formula of [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]], with the partial derivatives computed from the explicit expressions and the energy computed from its definition.

(i) For the constant source $h=1$ the spherical mean is $M_{cs}h(\cdot,v)(x)=1$ because $\int_{S^2}d\Omega=4\pi$ ([[lem-em-spherical-mean-wave-identity]]); the source integral is $c^2\int_0^t(t-v)\,dv=c^2t^2/2$ and the two homogeneous terms vanish because $a=b=0$. The time derivatives are read off the polynomial $c^2t^2/2$ with the algebra of derivatives ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]); $\Delta u=0$ because $u$ is independent of $x$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]). A nonzero constant function on $\mathbb R^3$ does not vanish off any compact set, so it is not compactly supported.

(ii) With $h(x,t)=h_0(x)$ the mean $M_{c(t-v)}h_0(x)$ is an integral over the sphere $S_{c(t-v)}(x)$ of $h_0$; if $|x|>1+c(t-t_0)$ then for every $v\in[t_0,t]$ every point of that sphere has norm at least $|x|-c(t-v)>1$, so the integrand vanishes identically on the sphere and the mean is $0$ ([[lem-em-spherical-mean-wave-identity]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Hence every term of the formula for $u(x,t)$ vanishes.

(iii) The first-moment lemma states $\int_{S^2}\omega\,d\sigma(\omega)=0$ for the polar surface measure ([[lem-first-moment-of-the-unit-sphere-vanishes]]), and [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]] identifies it with the surface measure used in $M$; therefore $M_{cs}b(x)=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{S^2}(x_1+cs\,n_1)\,d\Omega(n)=x_1$. Then $H_b(x,s)=sx_1$ and the other two terms vanish; differentiating $(t-t_0)x_1$ in $t$ twice and in $x$ twice gives $\partial_t^2u=0$ and $\Delta u=0$ ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]), so $Wu=0$, and the initial values are read off at $t=t_0$. For the energy, factor the box integral in the nonnegative Lebesgue integral ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]]) and evaluate the one-variable integral $\int_{-R}^Rx_1^2\,dx_1=2R^3/3$ ([[thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative]]); monotonicity of the nonnegative integral ([[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]) bounds the energy over $\mathbb R^3$ below by the box expression, which tends to $+\infty$; [[def-wave-energy-and-energy-flux]] supplies the energy density and the convention that an infinite integral means total energy $+\infty$. The solution's unboundedness on each slice $t>t_0$ is immediate from the expression $(t-t_0)x_1$.
